paragraphs: R' Prozdak bar Nachsha, at the beginning of Midrash Tehillim, chapter 91; Yalkut Tehillim 751 reads R' Prozdri bar Nachsha.[^1]

notes.text: רפצ״א is read contextually as beginning of chapter 91, not end. רמו is preserved as the supplied siglum, interpreted in context as a remez marker, without repairing Hebrew to רמז. תשנא totals 751, not 851. The Yalkut Prozdri versus Prozdak difference is Hyman’s reported variant, without fresh edition collation or identity merger. Both personal title abbreviations remain R'.
